title: Spiny chondrichthyan from the lower Silurian of South China
authors: Andreev, P.S.; Sansom, I.J.; Li, Q.; Zhao, W.; Wang, J.; Wang, C.-C.; Peng, L.; Jia, L.; Qiao, T.; Zhu, M.
note: The taxon is based on isolated dermal elements and fused skeletal fragments rather than an articulated body or associated dentition.

title: The oldest complete jawed vertebrates from the early Silurian of China
authors: Zhu, Y.; Li, Q.; Lu, J.; Chen, Y.; Wang, J.; Gai, Z.; Zhao, W.; Wei, G.; Yu, Y.; Ahlberg, P.E.; Zhu, M.
note: Describes the articulated Chongqing Lagerstätte material; Xiushanosteus has multiple referred specimens, whereas Shenacanthus is known from one holotype.

title: A lamprey from the Devonian period of South Africa
authors: Gess, R.W.; Coates, M.I.; Rubidge, B.S.
note: The event is restricted to the holotype anatomy and Famennian occurrence; lifecycle and feeding behaviour are not directly preserved.

title: A Paleozoic stem hagfish Myxinikela siroka—revised anatomy and implications for evolution of the living jawless vertebrate lineages
note: Revision based on the holotype and a newly reported paratype; preservation differs between specimens and several structures remain equivocal.

title: Hagfish from the Cretaceous Tethys Sea and a reconciliation of the morphological–molecular conflict in early vertebrate phylogeny
authors: Miyashita, T.; Coates, M.I.; Farrar, R.; Larson, P.; Manning, P.L.; Wogelius, R.A.; Edwards, N.P.; Anné, J.; Bergmann, U.; Palmer, A.R.; Currie, P.J.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Primary source for the Cenomanian crown-hagfish context used by the Myxini navigation range; it is not one of the seven focal events.

title: Lower Cambrian vertebrates from south China
authors: Shu, D.-G.; Luo, H.-L.; Conway Morris, S.; Zhang, X.-L.; Hu, S.-X.; Chen, L.; Han, J.; Zhu, M.; Li, Y.; Chen, L.-Z.
note: Primary descriptions of Myllokunmingia and Haikouichthys from the Chengjiang biota; their agnathan-grade interpretation is historical and does not establish a monophyletic Agnatha crown or direct ancestry.

title: Conodont affinity and chordate phylogeny
authors: Donoghue, P.C.J.; Forey, P.L.; Aldridge, R.J.
note: A systematic review of conodont biological affinity and chordate relationships, not a precise clade-origin date.

title: The phylogeny of the Craniata, with particular reference to the significance of fossil ‘agnathans’
note: Treats traditional ostracoderms as multiple armored jawless lineages rather than one natural clade.

title: A phylogeny for Heterostraci (stem-gnathostomes)
authors: Randle, E.; Keating, J.N.; Sansom, R.S.
note: A whole-group morphology matrix; topology does not directly establish the group's global range.

title: Phylogeny, classification and character polarity of the Osteostraci (Vertebrata)
note: A comprehensive genus-level morphology analysis, not a direct age determination.

title: 28S and 18S rDNA sequences support the monophyly of lampreys and hagfishes
note: An extant sequence topology; it does not set fossil first appearances or divergence time.

title: Lampreys as Diverse Model Organisms in the Genomics Era
authors: McCauley, D.W.; Docker, M.F.; Whyard, S.; Li, W.
note: A synthesis of living lamprey diversity and genomics, not an order-wide fossil range study.

title: Two new species of Dunkleosteus Lehman, 1956, from the Ohio Shale Formation (USA, Famennian) and the Kettle Point Formation (Canada, Upper Devonian), and a cladistic analysis of the Eubrachythoraci (Placodermi, Arthrodira)
publisher: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society
note: A eubrachythoracid sample nested within Arthrodira; it is not a complete order history.
